Strategy: Largest-bin shield: score by tightest fit but subtract a large penalty from the single largest feasible bin whenever another bin exists, so the roomiest bin is preserved for a future item that only it can fit. It can fail when the shielded bin is never needed and tight bins get overused instead.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    m = max(bins)
    return [(-(r - item) - (500.0 if (r == m and len(bins) > 1) else 0.0)) for r in bins]
```
